name: Thinking Walk
title: Take a daily walk on a fixed route with one problem loaded.
benefit: Clearer thinking on problems that resist the desk.
subtitle: Problem Solving
rationale: A known route removes navigation decisions, which frees attention to work on the problem while the body moves.
origin: Paul Graham walks a fixed route with one problem loaded.

evidence.summary: Experiments show walking acutely boosts creative ideation; the fixed-route, problem-loaded format is practitioner design.

sources.label: Paul Graham, How to Do Great Work

indications: A hard problem has resisted desk time for days.
Walks happen but are filled with podcasts and calls.
